text:
marie_p: Heads-up — Sales opened a private-deploy intake from Silverline Financial. They want a VPC-hosted private control plane (no public internet egress), HSM-backed KMS, cert pinning, and an on-prem MSSQL connector. Asking for an accelerated timeline due to contract renewal. Can we triage feasibility + launch criteria? :eyes:

sales_raj: raw ask from the customer below:
"We need Redwood private in our AWS VPC (us-east-1), private control plane only, HSM for key storage (YubiHSM or Azure Dedicated HSM), no model artifacts leaving our VPC, MS SQL connector to pull embeddings, 99.9% SLA for inference endpoints, must be able to pin model versions. Want go-live before renewal (10 weeks)."

alex_support: I linked the support ticket (S-4682) and included the customer's network diagram they sent. Low volume to start but they expect burst testing post-launch.

sam_soleng: Initial thoughts — doable but has several blockers. Need: customer CIDR ranges, NAT/Egress rules, whether they accept an outbound-only control channel, HSM vendor + integration method (PKCS#11 vs cloud KMS API), and persistent storage option (S3 vs NFS).

jamie_eng: Tech constraints to flag: our private control plane currently expects outbound TLS to Redwood artifact repos for model pull. For zero-egress we need a vendor-hosted artifact mirror or on-prem model hosting. Also need to confirm GPU availability on their side if they want runtime on-prem. Quantized models reduce footprint but we must verify model QA.

tess_sec: Security checklist items: HSM attestation, yearly key rotation policy, audit log export (SIEM integration), cert lifecycle (must support cert pinning/rotation), and pentest window. Also: we require a service account mapping and RBAC agreement. :lock:

deploy-bot: NOTE: Private deployment playbook v2.1 requires the following fields before a feasibility spike is scheduled: network_cidr, contact_for_ops, hsm_vendor, storage_type, data_residency_statement.

marie_p: Proposal for acceptance/launch criteria (draft):
- Signed enterprise contract with Dedicated capacity commit or Private license (min 6mo).
- Customer provides CIDR, firewall rules, and KMS/HSM access plan.
- HSM compatibility confirmed (PKCS#11 or supported cloud HSM).
- Model artifact hosting plan (mirror repo or on-prem blob).
- Onboarding runbook + SRE playbook agreed.
- Security review complete and pentest scheduled.

marie_p: Timeline estimate (rough):
- VPC private control plane only: 8–12 weeks (reqs + infra + validation).
- Add HSM integration + audit: +3–4 weeks.
- Air-gapped / fully on-prem runtime: +6–8 weeks (additional infra & QA).

alex_support: Customer requested 10 weeks — that maps to the VPC-only path if no HSM and if they accept outbound control plane. If they insist on HSM and no egress, timeline will slip.

sales_raj: Can we offer a compromise: start with VPC private control plane (outbound to Redwood repo) and then migrate HSM/airgap as phase 2? They want contract flexibility to add HSM after initial rollout.

jamie_eng: That's the pragmatic path. Phase 1 = control plane + model pinning + MSSQL connector (we can run a proxied connector if they allow a narrow outbound). Phase 2 = HSM + artifact mirror + full zero-egress if they require it.

sam_soleng: Dependencies checklist (relay to customer):
- Network: customer CIDR, peering/VPN details, allowed ports
- KMS/HSM: vendor, integration method, test credentials
- Storage: s3 endpoint or NFS details for model artifacts
- Auth: SAML/OIDC config for SSO + service account for control plane
- Compliance: SOC/ISO docs, data residency confirmation
- Ops contacts: primary ops + escalation contact

sam_soleng: sample minimal firewall snippet for Phase 1:
```
Inbound: 443 (control plane agent)
Inbound: 50051 (internal gRPC, optional)
Outbound: 443 -> our artifact repo and control endpoints
```

marie_p: Prioritization question — do we accept this into the product backlog pipeline (standard intake) or route it immediately to Enterprise ENG track (requires dedicated engineering SLA + commercial commitment)?

tess_sec: From a security/compliance POV, anything with HSM and zero-egress should go enterprise track. Lower risk if they accept outbound.

alex_support: The customer is signaled to be an upsell and a reference in financial vertical. Sales willing to commit to a 12mo dedicated capacity if we can promise a go-live window.

marie_p: Suggested next actions:
1) Sales collects the dependency answers from Silverline by EOD Thursday (CIDRs, HSM vendor, storage plan, SSO). // @sales_raj
2) Solutions drafts HSM compatibility matrix and a Phase 1/Phase 2 rollout plan (2 business days). // @sam_soleng
3) Engineering to schedule a 2-week feasibility spike (slot if product OK). // @jamie_eng
4) Security to pre-check HSM vendors against our policy and note gaps. // @tess_sec
5) Product to make go/no-go decision in next Triage meeting (Thu). // @marie_p :calendar:

sales_raj: I'll ping Silverline and chase the checklist today. If we can get answers this week we can try for the 2-week spike next Mon. :rocket:

jamie_eng: I'll prep a short spike scope doc listing tests: artifact mirror test, model pinning, MSSQL connector PoC, HSM PKCS#11 handshake.

tess_sec: I'll start a vendor risk mini-assessment for the two HSMs they named (YubiHSM, Azure Dedicated HSM).

marie_p: Great — keep updates here. If we get the dependency list, I'll slot this into the backlog and tag as enterprise-track with tentative timeline. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: ACTION_REQUIRED: add "silverline_financial" intake to private-deploy queue and attach S-4682.

alex_support: noted, I'll attach logs and the customer's network diagram.

sales_raj: thanks team. Will update by EOD. :pray:
